catalog_title: Is the specified generating series involving the number of distinct prime factors of an integer irrational?
original_question_en: Let omega(n) be the number of distinct prime factors of n. Is the series sum_{n>=1} omega(n)/2^n irrational? (Erdos 1948; settled conditionally by K. Pratt, arXiv:2409.15185, under a uniform prime k-tuples conjecture.)
lean_statement_sketch:
def omega (n : Nat) : Nat := (n.primeFactors).card
noncomputable def jsp87Series : Real := tsum fun n => ((omega n : Nat) : Real) * (2:Real)^-(n+1)
theorem jsp_000087_main : jsp87Series.Irrational

-- Round 40 added, in JSPProblem/Periodicity.lean and JSPProblem/LambertTrunc.lean, the full
-- unconditional apparatus of the Erdos--Pratt method on BOTH sides: the exact carry
-- recurrence theta_{N+1} = 2 theta_N - omega N, the uniform bound theta_N >= 1/4, the
-- aperiodicity of omega, the exact clearing denominator of the truncated Lambert sum, and
-- the Lambert-side denominator obstruction.
-- Round 41 added, in JSPProblem/DigitCarry.lean, the exact binary-digit bookkeeping of the carry excess: floor(2^N S) = I N + floor(theta N) (the binary floor is short of the 2-adic prefix by exactly the carry excess), I (N+1) = 2 I N + omega N, the doubling map on fractional parts, the from-scratch theorem that a rational's binary digits are eventually periodic, the identity d N = omega N + c(N+1) - 2 c N, and the endgame theorem 'eventually-periodic carry excess floor(2^N tau N) => jsp87Series is irrational' with its contrapositive.
-- Round 44 added, in JSPProblem/CarryExcess.lean, the QUANTITATIVE SHAPE of the carry excess c N = floor(theta N) and the unconditional sieve content of the correlation hypothesis: omega_ge_two_of_six_dvd and omega_unbounded (omega is unbounded), jsp87Carry_window_lower and jsp87Carry_ge_one_plus_seven (1 + 1/128 <= theta N for every N >= 2, so the carries are NEVER small and the classical 'theta N < 1/b' contradiction is impossible), jsp87CarryExcess_ge_omega and jsp87CarryExcess_unbounded (omega N < 2 c N + 2, hence c N is unbounded, with primorial instances), jsp87Series_irrational_of_carryExcess_bounded (a bounded carry excess would force irrationality, unconditionally, closing the carry-magnitude route in both directions), prod_ge_pow_card / card_largeFactors_le_log / jsp87_sum_omega_window_le (the large prime factors of a window are only logarithmically many) and jsp87_window_rough (for every m, L there is a window of length L with no prime factor in (L, m] -- the small primes of a window are controllable, only the large ones are not), plus the exact bridge jsp87Carry_split (theta N = sum_{k<L} omega (N+k) 2^-(k+1) + 2^-L theta (N+L)) and its corollaries jsp87Carry_le_window and jsp87Carry_le_smallFactors.
-- Round 46 added, in JSPProblem/BlockPeriod.lean, the QUANTITATIVE ARITHMETIC OF THE BASE-2
-- EXPANSION ITSELF -- the new attack family. The t-digit block of the Erdős series, read as a
-- binary integer: def jsp87DigitBlock (N t : Nat) : Int := sum_{j<t} jsp87Digit (N+j) * 2^(t-1-j).
-- jsp87_digitBlock_bounds : 0 <= B N t < 2^t (a block is a genuine t-bit integer);
-- jsp87_digitBlock_step / _shift : periodic digits make the block constant along the period,
--   B (N+q*t) t = B N t. jsp87_floor_telescope : the FINITE TELESCOPING IDENTITY
--   floor (2^(N+t) S) = 2^t * floor (2^N S) + B N t (Mathlib has no statement about the base-2
--   expansion of a real number at all), and jsp87_floor_block_iter : its iteration along the
--   period, (2^t - 1) * floor (2^(N+q*t) S) = 2^(t*q) * K - B N t.
-- THE MAIN THEOREM, jsp87_frac_scaled_eq_block : if the binary digits of S are eventually
--   periodic from N with period t > 0 then Int.fract (2^N * S) = B N t / (2^t - 1). This is
--   the QUANTITATIVE form of 'a rational has eventually periodic binary digits': the
--   denominator of the fractional part is exactly 2^t - 1 (the PERIOD) and the numerator is
--   exactly the digit block. It is the missing half of the Erdos--Pratt method: rounds 38/40
--   only said rationality freezes the carries into (1/b)Z, round 46 says the freeze is explicit.
-- jsp87_period_denominator_obstruction : if S = a/b (b>0) and the digits are eventually
--   periodic with period t, then (2^t - 1) divides b * B N t -- the period-denominator
--   obstruction, pinning the hypothetical rational from above (round 39's
--   dvd_lambert_den_prime_gt pins it from below). jsp87Series_irrational_of_frac_notPeriodic
--   and jsp87Series_rational_imp_frac_periodic : the fractional-part criterion, both directions.
-- jsp87Series_rational_imp_blockConst : the three rigidity conclusions together.

-- Round 51 added, in JSPProblem/PeriodEquation.lean, the PERIOD EQUATION and the
-- omega-WINDOW arithmetic: the t-step form of the carry recurrence with the
-- inhomogeneous term read off, omega N t = sum_{j<t} omega (N+j) 2^(t-1-j) --
-- a weighted average of the omega-values of t consecutive integers, the object a
-- prime-k-tuples correlation hypothesis is supposed to control.  37 new theorems
-- and 4 new definitions, 0 sorry, 0 admit; 488 proved theorems and lemmas in the

-- increment), jsp87OmegaDiff, jsp87OmegaDiffWindow.  Key results:
-- jsp87Carry_iter (theta (N+t) = 2^t theta N - omega N t, the t-step carry
-- recurrence), jsp87CarryShift_step (THE PERIOD EQUATION, step form, UNCONDITIONAL:
-- omega (N+t) - omega N = 2*Delta N - Delta (N+1), so the whole omega-family is

-- digits the lag-t carry increment equals the lag-t carry-EXCESS increment, an
-- exact integer identity), jsp87_window_periodEquation ((2^t-1) theta N = (c
-- (N+t) - c N) + omega N t), jsp87_carry_block_equation (the same
-- quantisation in block form, (2^t-1) theta N = (2^t-1) c N + B N t),
-- jsp87_window_block_equation (THE HEADLINE: c (N+t) + omega N t = 2^t c N + B
-- N t -- the first exact integer equation in the tree involving a window of
-- omega-values), jsp87_window_block_congr (THE WINDOW CONGRUENCE: 2^t - 1
-- divides c (N+t) - c N + omega N t - B N t, quotient exactly c N -- the first
-- divisibility statement in the carry family and the first time a Mersenne
-- number divides an expression built from omega-values),
-- jsp87_carryExcess_window_le (c (N+t) <= 2^t c N),
-- jsp87_omegaWindow_le_carryExcess (omega N t <= 2^t c N + 2^t - 1),
-- jsp87_omega_diff_periodEquation (THE PERIOD EQUATION on the omega-family: the
-- lag-t omega-difference is exactly the second difference of the carry excess),
-- jsp87_omega_diff_periodEquation_bound (|omega (N+t) - omega N| <= 6 log_2 (N+t+1)
-- under eventual periodicity), jsp87_dyadic_iff_carryInt (S = n/2^M iff the
-- carry theta M is an integer), jsp87_carryInt_iff_digitZero (hence the binary
-- digits of S are eventually 0 iff some carry is an integer -- the period-1
-- sub-case in carry language), jsp87_carry_int_ge_two (under the dyadic
-- hypothesis c N >= 2, unconditionally c N >= 1), jsp87_dyadic_omega_eq (under
-- the dyadic hypothesis omega N = 2 c N - c (N+1): the whole omega-family is a
-- doubling-difference of the carry excess), jsp87_dyadic_omega_bounds (the
-- squeeze 2 c N - log_2(N+1) <= omega N <= 2 c N - 2),
-- jsp87Series_irrational_of_omegaWindow_never_congr (THE FIFTH IRRATIONALITY
-- CRITERION: if no candidate period passes the window congruence test, S is

-- Round 52 added, in JSPProblem/AdicPrefix.lean, the 2-ADIC AND MODULAR ARITHMETIC

-- N-th partial sum, the integer whose binary expansion is the first N digits of S and

-- <-> 2^t | Omega N t (THE 2-ADIC WINDOW EQUIVALENCE).  Headline:
-- jsp87_prefix_mod_not_eventuallyPeriodic -- the binary prefix is APERIODIC MODULO
-- EVERY m >= 2, a sixth independent aperiodicity statement in the tree and the first
-- on this object, proved from round 49's aperiodicity of omega modulo every m >= 2 by
-- the transfer lemma jsp87Prefix_periodic_imp_omega_periodic (which uses the recursion

-- jsp87Val2_prefix_succ_even (v (I (N+1)) = v (I N + omega N / 2) + 1); the parity and
-- chain theorems jsp87Prefix_parity / jsp87Prefix_dvd_two_iff /
-- jsp87Prefix_dvd_pow_succ; the escape statement
-- jsp87_prefix_dvd_pow_two_not_eventually (the prefix escapes every fixed power of 2

-- jsp87_adic_carry_congr, the first statement reading the 2-adic content of the binary

-- 2^t | I (N+t) <-> 2^t | (c (N+t) - B N t).

notes:
ROUND 40 -- TWO NEW ATTACK FAMILIES, 42 NEW THEOREMS. The Lean tree is zero-sorry with 158 proved lemmas/theorems (was 116). (1) lean/JSPProblem/Periodicity.lean (NEW, 413 lines, 21 theorems): THE CARRY DYNAMICS AND THE APERIODICITY ENDGAME. jsp87Carry is the rescaled tail theta_N = 2^N * tau N and jsp87Carry_succ is the EXACT carry recurrence theta_{N+1} = 2 theta_N - omega N (with omega_eq_two_carry_sub recovering the digit from two consecutive carries). From the k=1 term of the tail, jsp87Carry_ge_omega_succ : omega(N+1) <= 4*theta_N, hence the sharp uniform bound jsp87Carry_ge_quarter : theta_N >= 1/4 for EVERY cut point N. This is new NEGATIVE knowledge and is the precise reason the naive Erdos argument cannot close: rationality freezes the carries into (1/b)Z but the carries are NOT confined to (0,1). Quantitatively, jsp87Carry_gt_one / _ge_half / _ge_three_halves turn omega(N+1) >= 5,2,6 into theta_N > 1, >= 1/2, >= 3/2. On the positive side jsp87_fract_scaled identifies fract(2^N S) = fract(theta_N) and jsp87_fract_scaled_eq_div shows that a rational S = a/b confines those fractional parts to a FINITE set of size b (via Int.fract_eq_div_of_mul_natCast, the general statement that b * fract x is an integer in [0,b) whenever b*x is an integer). Finally omega_not_eventuallyPeriodic is proved FROM SCRATCH: under an eventual period t, n |-> omega(t*n) is eventually CONSTANT (omega_eventuallyPeriodic_const_mul), but for M = N+1 and a prime u > t*M the number t*M*u lies in the same frozen progression while having one more prime factor (omega_mul_prime_of_large_prime), a contradiction. Mathlib has no aperiodicity statement for omega. (2) lean/JSPProblem/LambertTrunc.lean (NEW, 433 lines, 21 theorems): THE JOIN between the Lambert reduction (round 37) and the Lambert denominator arithmetic (round 39), which had never been made. jsp87_lambertTrunc_mul_den proves that the clearing denominator D_N = prod_{p<N}(2^p-1) is an EXACT INTEGER MULTIPLIER of the truncated prime-Lambert sum T_N = sum_{p<N} 1/(2^p-1) -- each (2^p-1) divides D_N, so D_N/(2^p-1) is a natural number -- and jsp87_lambertTrunc_eq_div gives T_N = numer_N / D_N. This is exactly the integrality step an Erdos-style irrationality argument needs. Analytically, jsp87_lambert_decomp gives 2*S = T_N + R_N, jsp87_lambertTail_pos proves the Lambert tail is strictly positive (a prime exists past every cut point) and jsp87_lambertTail_le gives 0 < R_N <= 4*2^-N. Arithmetically, jsp87_lambert_rat_obstruction proves the LAMBERT MIRROR of jsp87_carry_mul_eq_int: if 2*S = a/b with b>0 then b*D_N*R_N is a POSITIVE integer, hence >= 1; together with the tail bound this squeezes the cleared tail into jsp87_lambert_window : 1/(b*D_N) <= R_N <= 4*D_N*2^-N. ROUND 40 also CORRECTS the round-37/39 claim that the unconditional apparatus was 'complete': it was not, because the integrality of the cleared Lambert truncation was missing. And ACCEPTANCE.md's stated blocker is now sharper: with jsp87Carry_ge_quarter, the object that needs quantitative control is the INTERNAL CARRY floor(2^N * tau N), i.e. how much genuine carrying the series performs -- not theta_N itself. STILL MISSING: jsp_000087_main, the headline irrationality statement. It is CONDITIONAL in the published literature (Pratt arXiv:2409.15185, under a uniform prime k-tuples conjecture) and the catalog records 'Solved; Lean proof: No; Eligible to claim: No'. Declaring a weakened statement under that name would misrepresent the catalog headline, so the name is deliberately withheld.
ROUND 41: ONE NEW MODULE, JSPProblem/DigitCarry.lean (636 lines, 34 new theorems/defs, 0 sorry, 0 admit). The Lean tree now has 205 proved declarations and builds clean. New proved content: (i) the digit window jsp87Carry_window (sum_{k<=m} omega(N+k) 2^(m-k) <= 2^(m+1) theta N) and the concrete first carry jsp87CarryExcess_five_ge_one : 1 <= floor(theta 5); (ii) the 2-adic prefix recurrence jsp87IntPart_succ and the MISSING LINK jsp87_floor_scaled : floor (2^N S) = I N + floor(theta N); (iii) Int.fract_two_mul and jsp87_fract_scaled_succ (the doubling map on fractional parts, absent from Mathlib), jsp87Digit, jsp87_digit_eq_fract, jsp87Digit_mem; (iv) the exact integer identity jsp87_digit_bookkeeping : d N = omega N + c(N+1) - 2 c N; (v) jsp87_digit_eventuallyPeriodic, i.e. a rational number has eventually periodic binary digits, proved FROM SCRATCH (finite range + pigeonhole + the deterministic doubling map) because Mathlib has no such statement; (vi) the ENDGAME: jsp87Series_irrational_of_carryExcess_eventuallyPeriodic (eventual periodicity of the carry excess floor(2^N tau N) forces irrationality), its corollaries for the sub-case 'carries < 1 eventually' and 'excess stabilises', the contrapositive jsp87Series_rational_imp_carryExcess_not_periodic, and the dichotomy jsp87Series_irrational_or_carryExcess_not_periodic. The headline jsp_000087_main is STILL WITHHELD: the result is conditional in the literature (Pratt arXiv:2409.15185 needs a uniform prime k-tuples hypothesis) and the catalog itself records 'Solved; Lean proof: No; Eligible to claim: No'. After round 41 the remaining gap is a single object -- a quantitative estimate for the carry excess floor(2^N tau N) strong enough to contradict rationality.

ROUND 44 -- NEW ATTACK FAMILY: the quantitative shape of the carry excess + the unconditional sieve content of the correlation hypothesis. lean/JSPProblem/CarryExcess.lean (776 lines, 30 new theorems/defs, 0 sorry, 0 admit; 219 proved theorems and lemmas in the tree, lake build clean). The main output is NEGATIVE knowledge that closes the carry-magnitude strategy in both directions: (a) jsp87Carry_ge_one_plus_seven proves 1 + 1/128 <= theta N for EVERY cut point N >= 2 (every six consecutive integers contain a multiple of 6, which has two distinct prime factors, while every N+k >= 2 has one; combined with round 41's digit window this is a uniform bound), so the classical Erdos contradiction 'some cut point has theta N < 1/b' is FALSE for this series -- rationality only forces b*theta N in Z, i.e. theta N >= 1/b, and theta N is always > 1; (b) jsp87CarryExcess_ge_omega proves omega N < 2*floor(theta N) + 2, hence jsp87CarryExcess_unbounded: the carry excess is unbounded (instances at the primorials 210, 2310, 30030, 510510), and jsp87Series_irrational_of_carryExcess_bounded shows that a BOUNDED carry excess would force irrationality with no rationality hypothesis (bounded excess => bounded theta => omega bounded <= 2C+1, contradicting the new omega_unbounded). The second half attacks the object ACCEPTANCE.md names as the blocker -- 'quantitative correlations of omega at shifted points' -- and proves its unconditional content: prod_ge_pow_card (generalised product bound, base b >= 2), card_largeFactors_le_log (the prime factors of n exceeding m number at most log_m n), jsp87_sum_omega_window_le (the omega-profile of a window is controlled by its small prime factors plus one L*log_m(N+L) term), and jsp87_window_rough (for every m, L there is a window of length L in which NO integer has a prime factor in (L, m] -- the primes in (L, m] are avoided by the single congruence N = 1 mod prod_{L<p<=m} p because 1+k <= L < p). So the SMALL primes of a window are fully controllable and only the LARGE ones are not: that is precisely the unconditional half of Pratt's prime-k-tuples hypothesis, and the log_m bound is all that is known unconditionally about the other half. Finally the two halves are joined by the exact carry split jsp87Carry_split (theta N = sum_{k<L} omega (N+k) 2^-(k+1) + 2^-L theta (N+L)) with corollaries jsp87Carry_le_window and jsp87Carry_le_smallFactors. jsp_000087_main is STILL deliberately not declared: the round-44 theorems are negative knowledge plus the unconditional sieve content of the hypothesis, and none of them supplies the missing input (a statement strong enough to make the carry excess eventually periodic, equivalently the binary digits of S aperiodic). The catalog records 'Solved; Lean proof: No; Eligible to claim: No' and the published result is conditional on a uniform prime k-tuples conjecture, so no honest unconditional proof exists; the gate correctly reports partial_ok=true, prize_ready=false, missing_theorems=['jsp_000087_main'].
ROUND 46 -- NEW ATTACK FAMILY: the binary block of the series and the period of a hypothetical rational. lean/JSPProblem/BlockPeriod.lean (615 lines, 17 new theorems and defs, 0 sorry, 0 admit; 236 proved theorems and lemmas in the tree, 219 before, lake build clean). Rounds 41 and 44 had proved only the FORWARD direction of the base-2 bookkeeping (rationality => eventually periodic binary digits). Round 46 proves the CONVERSE direction QUANTITATIVELY, which is what an Erdos--Pratt argument needs: not merely that the digits must be periodic, but exactly what they would be. (i) The new object jsp87DigitBlock N t = sum_{j<t} d (N+j) * 2^(t-1-j), the next t binary digits of S read as an integer, together with jsp87_digitBlock_bounds (0 <= B < 2^t: a block is a genuine t-bit integer), jsp87_digitBlock_step and jsp87_digitBlock_shift (periodic digits make the block constant along the period). (ii) jsp87_floor_telescope: the FINITE TELESCOPING IDENTITY floor (2^(N+t) S) = 2^t * floor (2^N S) + B N t -- the binary prefix after t further digits is the prefix at N shifted by t places, plus the block; Mathlib has no statement about the base-2 expansion of a real number at all -- and jsp87_floor_block_iter, its iteration along the period, (2^t - 1) * floor (2^(N+q*t) S) = 2^(t*q) K - B N t. (iii) THE MAIN THEOREM jsp87_frac_scaled_eq_block: if the binary digits are eventually periodic from N with period t > 0 then Int.fract (2^N S) = B N t / (2^t - 1). This is the quantitative form of 'a rational has eventually periodic binary digits' and the missing half of the method: rounds 38/40 only said rationality freezes the carries into (1/b)Z, round 46 says the freeze is EXPLICIT -- the denominator of the fractional part is exactly 2^t - 1 (the period) and the numerator is exactly the digit block. The proof is a squeeze: iterate the telescoping identity q times along the period, convert floors to x - fract x, the 2^(t*q) * 2^N * S term cancels, leaving (2^t-1) f_N - B N t = 2^(-t*q) ((2^t-1) f_{N+qt} - B N t), which is O(2^(-t*q)) while the left side is q-independent. Two reusable Mathlib-gap lemmas are recorded: exists_pow_lt_real (exists_pow_lt is stated for ordered GROUPS and does not apply to R; exists_pow_lt_of_lt_one does) and abs_eq_zero_of_forall_le (an elementary squeeze, no topology). (iv) THE ENDGAME: jsp87Series_irrational_of_frac_notPeriodic (if the fractional parts n |-> fract (2^n S) are not eventually periodic then S is irrational) and its converse jsp87Series_rational_imp_frac_periodic; jsp87_frac_scaled_block_const (under periodic digits the fractional part of 2^(N+q t) S is a single constant for all q); and jsp87_period_denominator_obstruction, the PERIOD-DENOMINATOR OBSTRUCTION: if S = a/b (b > 0) and the digits are eventually periodic with period t then (2^t - 1) | b * B N t. This pins the hypothetical rational from ABOVE (the period ties b to 2^t - 1) while round 39's dvd_lambert_den_prime_gt pins it from BELOW (a fixed b cannot keep dividing 2^p - 1 as p grows); the only escape is a period t growing with N, which 'eventually periodic from some fixed N' forbids. jsp87Series_rational_imp_blockConst bundles the three rigidity conclusions. jsp_000087_main is STILL deliberately not declared: the reduction is now complete and sharp, but the headline irrationality is CONDITIONAL in the published literature (Pratt arXiv:2409.15185, uniform prime k-tuples) and the catalog records 'Solved; Lean proof: No; Eligible to claim: No'. The single remaining lemma is named exactly in the new blocker below and in ACCEPTANCE.md round 46.

--   sum' n, [n prime] q^-(n+1) is irrational;

ROUND 50 -- NEW ATTACK FAMILY (ASYMPTOTIC CARRY THEORY), 68 NEW THEOREMS. New module lean/JSPProblem/CarryAsymptotic.lean (1010 lines, 68 new theorems/lemmas/defs, 0 sorry, 0 admit; 451 proved theorems and lemmas in the tree at the ^(theorem|lemma) level, 385 before this round; lake build clean). round50_blocker.statement: the number of 1-digits among the first N binary digits of the Erdős series, D N = sum_{M<N} jsp87Digit M, is bounded by NO linear function of N along an unbounded sequence; formally (forall C > 0) (forall K) (exists N >= K) D N > C * N

Equivalently, via jsp87_digitCount_eq_fractSum (D N + fract (2^N S) = S + sum_{M<N} fract (2^M S)) and round 41's jsp87_digit_eq_fract, the MEAN of the doubling orbit N |-> fract (2^N S) must fail to be bounded by any linear function.

round50_blocker.attack_family_this_round: ASYMPTOTIC CARRY THEORY -- new family. Rounds 37-46 attacked the carried series through periodicity (Lambert reduction, carry scaffold, gcd arithmetic, carry dynamics, digit bookkeeping, carry-excess/sieve content, base-2 block arithmetic), round 47 the carry-free (primary) expansion, round 48 the doubling map on the carries, round 49 the criterion in arbitrary radix. This round changes the QUESTION rather than the tool: how FAST can the carry excess grow, and how FAST does the binary digit string accumulate 1s. The single observation is that the carry is a geometrically weighted average of the omega-values after the cut point, so omega m <= log_2 m makes the carry SUBLINAR. Concretely: theta N = sum'_k omega (N+k) 2^{-(k+1)} (jsp87Carry_eq_tsum) and theta N <= log_2 N + log_2 e / N (jsp87Carry_le_logb_sharp) -- the FIRST sublinear upper bound on the carry (rounds 38-40 had only the linear theta N <= N+1). Combined with round 44's c N >= 1 and unboundedness this yields the LOGARITHMIC WINDOW jsp87CarryExcess_window: 1 <= c N <= k+3 for 2 <= N <= 2^{k+1}, and jsp87CarryExcess_unbounded_beyond: the carry excess escapes every such range.
